answer.generated: In object database systems, object-identifiers serve as pointers but are abstracted away from the logical level, making them invisible to users. This abstraction preserves the benefits of pointers—such as efficient referencing and handling of complex relationships—while maintaining the simplicity and consistency expected at the logical schema level. Thus, object-identifiers exhibit characteristics similar to pointers, enabling flexible data organization without exposing underlying implementation details.
